chunks: And in it, he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in the distribution of the khums.
But He is unjust to them in the distribution of the zakat.
ai.seo_question: How does divine justice differ between the distribution of khums and zakat?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this nuanced distinction to highlight that while the fixed rate of khums is divinely ordained and justly distributed to the Imam and the poor, the variable nature of zakat has historically been subject to human administrative discretion and potential inequity. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s authority ensures the perfect justice of khums, whereas zakat’s distribution often depended on the Caliphs' policies, leading to perceived injustices against the servants of Allah.
